source_review.notes: Checked current official NASA Systems Engineering Handbook pages for Stakeholder Expectations Definition, Technical Requirements Definition, Logical Decomposition, Design Solution Definition, Decision Analysis and Technical Assessment; the published ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 record; CMU SEI architecture-analysis guidance; NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1; and GAO-15-37. Eight final URLs returned HTTP 200 through direct command-line retrieval. ISO and GAO returned HTTP 403 to scripted curl but were independently retrieved through browser access on the review date and matched their current publication records and findings. Claims are limited to stakeholder/ConOps grounding, alternative design iteration, concerns and architecture descriptions, scenario-based trade analysis, lifecycle trustworthiness, comparable alternatives and independent challenge.

evidence: Reviewed alternative, stakeholder, scenario, concern, evidence and baseline sets; the constraint-defined feasible set; stakeholder-specific additive value model; decision-frame tuple; consequence indices; dominance relation and regret expression.
Confirmed every symbol is introduced and that alternatives, feasibility, consequences, preferences, risks, authority and history remain distinct.
Confirmed additive value is explicitly conditional on scale, independence and compensation assumptions and is not presented as a universal social-choice theorem.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The formalism structures a governed comparison but cannot establish legitimate authority, complete stakeholder coverage or an ethically acceptable choice.

evidence: Executed stakeholder-architecture-constraint-check and reproduced three alternatives and three mandatory constraints.

Recomputed central's sole outage_access failure (58 < 75), edge's sole safety failure (79 < 80), hybrid's absence of failures and hybrid as the only eligible alternative; all architectures satisfy the declared privacy threshold of 80.
Recomputed stakeholder values: authority central 81.2, edge 81.7, hybrid 84.3; operator central 84.6, edge 74.3, hybrid 82.2; community central 77.6, edge 83.5, hybrid 83.8.
Recomputed minimum stakeholder values central 77.6, edge 74.3 and hybrid 82.2, yielding hybrid under the declared feasibility-first teaching rule.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The 0–100 outcomes and weights are declared teaching values only; they are not clinical measurements, population estimates or authorized stakeholder preferences.

evidence: Confirmed that the feasible set requires every applicable mandatory inequality before preference comparison, so finite points cannot compensate for constraint failure.
Confirmed that stakeholder value is separately indexed by stakeholder and scenario and that weights sum to one within each declared model.
Confirmed that dominance requires no-worse comparable outcomes plus at least one strict improvement and is bounded by uncertainty.
Confirmed that regret and maximin-style summaries are diagnostic robustness aids rather than automatically authorized decision rules.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Selection remains conditional on valid constraints, comparable alternatives, credible consequence evidence and legitimate value governance.

evidence: Challenged customer-only stakeholder maps, homogeneous user averages, absent non-users/risk takers, weak representation, power imbalance, fabricated consensus and role confusion among participation, expertise, concurrence, authority and acceptance.

Reviewed solution-shaped needs, preference-versus-constraint errors, improper compensation, invalid ordinal arithmetic, nonlinear thresholds, correlated/double-counted criteria, post-result weights and illegitimate social aggregation.

Reviewed asymmetric alternatives, hidden enabling systems/labor, missing status quo/defer/staging/fallback, nominal-only scenarios, supplier benchmarks, unrepresentative studies, false precision, tails, common cause and subgroup harm.

Reviewed centralized, distributed and hybrid stereotypes; organizational feasibility, migration, reversibility, option value, readiness, safety/security/privacy, operations, cost/schedule and lifecycle burdens.
Reviewed no-acceptable-option outcomes, emergency/public decisions, sensitive evidence, implementation versus validation, stale premises and supersession rather than retrospective rewriting.

Reviewed all ten examples and five answers for configured scope, stakeholders, constraints, comparable architectures, evidence, distributions, uncertainty, dissent, authority, propagation and reopening.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real high-consequence selection requires applicable domain, stakeholder, community, safety, security, privacy, human-factors, accessibility, ethics, legal, regulatory, procurement, finance, organizational, supplier, operational and affected-risk-taker review.

evidence: Traced exact question, authority, configured baseline, lifecycle and reversibility from framing through decision record and supersession.
Confirmed stakeholder subgroups, representation, missing voices and risk takers remain visible rather than collapsing into a fictional average stakeholder.
Confirmed needs, values, objectives, constraints, requirements, concerns, scenarios, measures and preference functions remain linked but distinct.
Confirmed constraints precede preference aggregation, alternatives retain common scope/fidelity and evidence retains provenance, configuration, population, uncertainty, conflicts and limitations.
Confirmed recommendation, authority decision, dissent, residual risk, baseline propagation, implementation verification, outcome validation, monitoring and reopening remain separate governed steps.
invariant_checking.notes: A complete process does not guarantee that stakeholder inclusion, thresholds, values, evidence or authority are substantively legitimate; those remain review obligations.

proof_review.notes: The chapter defines comparison relations and invariants but presents no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed feasible, acceptable, safe, secure, private, representative, robust, dominated, preferred, validated, successful, fair and consensus language for bounded evidence and authority.
artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-050/report.json records exact local execution evidence for declared teaching values and arithmetic only.
The module requires source, version, configuration, workload/population, environment, method, uncertainty, conflicts, limitations and applicability for empirical claims.
Deployment, conformance, test passage, a high average score or independent challenge is never presented as proof of stakeholder outcome effectiveness or ethical acceptability.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external review is claimed. The teaching checker explicitly cannot establish real clinical safety, lawful authority, representativeness or acceptable values.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked architecture alternative, stakeholder, concern, value, quality-attribute scenario, constraint, criterion, value model, risk taker, dominance, distribution, robustness, authority and reopening. The module consistently frames architecture as allocation of control, failure, information, labor, cost, exposure and options, not merely structure or technology.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked decision framing, stakeholder power/representation, scenario construction, constraint governance, comparable whole alternatives, provenance, field and model evidence, preference elicitation, distributions, uncertainty/sensitivity, organizational feasibility, readiness/risk, independent challenge, decision records, configuration propagation and outcome monitoring. Cases span clinical support, rail, public identity, services, flood warning, governed data, factories, microgrids, supplier platforms and protected pilots.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed that this Level I capstone retrieves and integrates system definition, stakeholder, architecture, interface, trade, uncertainty, readiness, risk and decision-record skills. Ten distinct examples and five complete solutions require learners to build evidence/governance packages, analyze a public heat-response system, explain constraint-first selection, repair a biased study and supersede a failed hybrid architecture.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, systems-engineering, architecture, clinical, safety, security, privacy, human-factors, accessibility, ethics, legal, regulatory, public-sector, emergency-management, procurement, finance, organizational, supplier, operations, verification, validation, community, equity, or affected-risk-taker review is claimed.
